questions.q: Why are large data files and trained model binaries usually kept out of a normal Git repository?
options: Git cannot store files that end in .csv or .joblib
Git keeps every version of every file forever, so large binary files that change often bloat the repository, and GitHub blocks files over 100 MiB
Because data files are always confidential
Because models cannot be reproduced
questions.explain: Every committed version stays in history. Dedicated data and model versioning (Chapter 2) is a better fit than Git for large binary artifacts.

questions.q: In the lesson, models/metrics.json is left tracked while models/*.joblib is ignored. Why?
options: metrics.json is small, and tracking it records each commit's score next to its settings
JSON files cannot be ignored by .gitignore
The joblib file contains no useful information
GitHub requires a JSON file in every repository
questions.explain: Small result files diff well and let the commit history show settings and outcomes together.

questions.q: Re-running one notebook cell changed only the execution count, yet git diff showed the file as modified. What does nbstripout do about this?
options: It prevents notebooks from running
It converts notebooks to Word documents
It deletes the notebook from the working directory
It strips outputs and counters from the version Git stores, while your working copy keeps them
questions.explain: As a Git clean filter, nbstripout removes outputs and execution counts at staging time; the file on disk is untouched.

questions.q: The tune-C branch raised accuracy from 0.768 to 0.776 on a 250-row test set. What is the right reading of that result?
options: Proof that C=10 is the best possible setting
Evidence that Git measures model quality
A difference of two customers, so too small to trust without better evaluation and tracking
A sign the test set was leaked
questions.explain: 0.008 of 250 rows is two predictions. Git records what you tried, but it cannot judge whether the change is real.

questions.q: What is a pull request template for ML changes good for?
options: Automatically training the model on GitHub
Storing the dataset in the pull request
Making reviewers see settings, before-and-after metrics and data details in a consistent checklist
Removing the need for code review
questions.explain: A template in .github/pull_request_template.md prompts authors to include what reviewers need to judge an ML change.
